From Adalat O Ekti Meye (1981) to The Accused (1988) to Damini (1993) and Dahan (1997), the courtroom drama has  a solid tradition of revealing the prurience of the legal system. The Hindi film Section 375 is a sly anomaly dismissing the #MeToo movement

Where judges are thoughtful, lawyers are decent and the woman is lying about rape: the Hindi film's sly post #MeToo stance

#MeToo is itself a vigilante response to the savage misogyny in the legal system, nicely drawn out in the courtroom drama as a genre. It gives rise to the other rape genre--the rape revenge film like Kaabil, MOM, Bhoomi. MeToo is a similar guerilla tactic https://t.co/MjWaGkQJYe

What witch-hunt? Who was burnt at the stake? Men are still making unfunny jokes that they laugh at loudly and commenting on our bodies, also tutoring their partners to do it on their behalf #MeToo

Bollywood's response to #MeToo is to dismiss the movement with nastiness ~ in #Super30 sexual misconduct accused Vikas Bahl says women who complain of sexual harassment are liars. In #section375 lawyers are decent, the court is sensitive but women are lying about rape >>

There is a tradition of films on rape/sexual assault and the courtroom drama, which is progressive, feminist and aware of the problems with "due process". It exists in Hindi film, Bengali film and in Hollywood. But in the post #MeToo moment, Bollywood feels courts are enough
